quote: electricity bills that we're getting, and rates are just gonna continue to go up.
stewart_read: This is the emotional anchor for the whole call and it's never referenced again — rep never flips 'rates are going to keep going up' into urgency for booking.
coaching_implication: Rep should have circled back at bill collection or program pitch: 'that's exactly why locking in now protects you from those rate increases you mentioned.'

quote: I'm just a scheduler, so I don't know too much.
stewart_read: Rep names her own scope limit accurately, then immediately breaks it by explaining the bill-swap mechanism in detail.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep felt she had to fill the silence/answer to keep the customer engaged rather than losing her to specialist redirect.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch verbatim: bridge to specialist instead of self-explaining product mechanics.

quote: what are you talking about as far as an amount that would be due for the solar bill?
stewart_read: Customer's genuine pricing question gets a full mechanical explanation (kWh, bar graph, panel count) instead of a curiosity-preserving redirect to the specialist appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may have judged that answering builds trust before asking for the appointment. But no appointment ask follows, so the trust wasn't converted.
coaching_implication: Answer at a high level, then pivot: 'that's exactly what our specialist will map out with your actual numbers — let's get that on the calendar.'

quote: I believe it can. Yeah. I mean, I know some people that I've worked with, they some of them have super cheap bills now where they are they're only paying, like, $15 a month.
stewart_read: Rep cites a specific unverified dollar figure from anecdote to answer a pricing question — a numeric-discipline risk and further scope creep.
coaching_implication: Avoid quoting other customers' bills as a proxy answer; redirect pricing specifics to the specialist.

quote: I I really don't know. That is a really good question, and I can notate that down for my specialist as well.
stewart_read: The one moment the rep correctly admits the limit and defers transparently instead of fabricating.
coaching_implication: This is the model move — do this from the first program question, not the fourth.

quote: Okay. I'll see what I can do. I mean, tomorrow is Saturday, so they're not gonna be I can't get a hold of anybody until Monday at their earliest.
stewart_read: Customer surfaces a real timing constraint (utility closed until Monday) and the rep never converts this into a scheduled callback time or appointment.
coaching_implication: Should have locked: 'Great, I'll call you Monday afternoon once you've reached them — does 2pm work?' instead of leaving it open-ended.
